hypothesis: Training a 12k-parameter low-rank readout residual on the existing 100M generative model improves strict answer accuracy over the frozen parent across independently withheld RU/EN arithmetic, code and memory examples.
adapter_architecture: post-final-RMSNorm residual low-rank 768->8->768; no symbolic solver, no parser at inference
training: verified L100A synthetic memory+replay; same exact tokenizer 8192; 50/50 each family group per minibatch, training examples pre-existing, no held used for updates
held_source: L100A datasets/regression.jsonl and iid.jsonl from previously frozen archive, no overlap with L100A train groups verified
evaluate: Same 160 prompts for frozen L100EC and final LoRA-adapted L100EC. Greedy full-vocabulary 24 generated tokens; only explicit F=<integer> with EOS counts correct; retain raw outputs, do not treat timeout as incorrect reference Qwen.
success: Strict exact answers increase by >=3 percentage points over parent across160 held questions; disclose per-family results and all EOS/format rates
limitations: Weight-only BF16-to-FP32 warm start. Tiny adapter cannot plausibly make the 100M model universally smarter than Qwen3.5-0.8B; no new Qwen run, no external held benchmark, old EC training leakage against L100A data not fully ruled out.
